sentences.span: AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: BofA (per this note) coins the term for the bond-breaks/equities-ignore split described through the rest of the article.

sentences.span: in a market with "a relatively fixed supply of attention", macro risk "is struggling to compete for attention with the growth potential of AI narratives." AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying
sentences.why: Direct paraphrase of BofA's stated mechanism.

sentences.span: the bond market is flashing red and the equity market is not listening
sentences.why: Editorial bridge sentence; stance reflects BofA's (s1/s2) and Goldman Pasquariello's (s4/s5) documented, differing framings of what the bond market move means — no new fact asserted.

sentences.span: in the absence of an inflation surge -- or a credit problem ... I view higher rates as a headwind to stocks, NOT as a wrecking ball
sentences.why: Direct match to Pasquariello's stated view.

sentences.span: when 10-year notes back up 2 standard deviations in one month's time, S&P usually begins to show some strain ... the "speed limit" is most acute when it's driven by a surge in real yields
sentences.why: The 'speed limit'/2-std-dev-in-a-month rule is about pace, not absolute yield level, matching the sentence's framing.

sentences.span: I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here
sentences.why: Three-item checklist for adding net equity risk, verbatim content match.

sentences.span: The French 10-year OAT yield climbed to around 4.92-4.95%, its highest in roughly two decades, and the spread over Bunds pushed through 140bps, the widest since the euro crisis of 2012
sentences.why: Verbatim match of yield level and spread/record framing.

sentences.span: Fair value for the 10y OAT-Bund spread stands at 100-110bp ... We cut our French growth forecasts again, to 0.3% and 0.6% for this year and next
sentences.why: BofA source matches both the fair-value spread and the growth-forecast cut exactly.

sentences.span: does Europe reap enough of the benefits from a growth perspective to be fine too? ... growth is just ~1%
sentences.why: Goldman Sachs (Codacci-Pisanelli) macro note poses exactly this question; correctly attributed to Goldman rather than to The Market Ear's separate roundup of the same chart.

sentences.span: signs of successful negotiations for the 2027 budget - keeping the deficit as close as possible to the government objective of 5.0% ... could offer support
sentences.why: Goldman names this as a resolving condition for the French spread stress, matching the falsifiable-condition framing.

sentences.span: 2026 projected hyperscaler issuance of $250bn ... most of this year's funding ($230bn) completed ... now expecting $420bn ... (vs. $400bn ...) ... 35% of 2027's hyperscaler CapEx spending will be debt funded
sentences.why: All four figures match Goldman Sachs credit desk note exactly.

sentences.span: it will require a hot September CPI print (due 14 October) to make the meeting interesting
sentences.why: Date and conditionality match; 'back into play' phrasing corroborated by a second source (MS Savone note, same day) saying a hot CPI print 'could bring October back into play.'

sentences.span: we are raising our price target to $820 from $750 that is now based on 25x our FY27 EPS estimate (previously 23x)

Muse has quickly become the #1 app in Productivity, with 4.9 stars among 38k ratings ... >3mn app installs in the US during its first 16 days ... ChatGPT ... took ~35 days to match Muse's cumulative [installs]
sentences.why: All figures (rank, rating, rating count, installs, days, ChatGPT comparison) match verbatim.

sentences.span: we do not think there is a large incentive for users to upgrade and subscribe to the higher tiers ... Muse could represent ~Mid-SD% of Meta's 2030 revenue ... we calculate roughly $25-$50 per Muse user in CapEx
sentences.why: Free-tier/upgrade-incentive framing, 2030 revenue percentage, and capex-per-user range all match the Deutsche Bank note.
